novel_features.name: Statute-citation graph
novel_features.description: List every locally-synced judgment that cites a given statute article, broken down by court and year. Use this when you need 'every High Court drug case that ever invoked §17(2)' in one query.
novel_features.rationale: Requires extracting statute references from judgment text into a citations table at sync — no Taiwan judicial API exposes this cross-judgment view; only commercial Lawsnote does, and that path is currently chilled by the 2024 verdict.
novel_features.example: judgementtw-pp-cli cites statute 毒品危害防制條例 --article 17 --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: An agent answering 'has any court ever ruled X under statute Y?' can resolve it in one structured call instead of paginating through hundreds of HTML pages.

novel_features.name: Reverse-citation precedent lookup
novel_features.description: Find judgments in the local store that cite a given JID. Surfaces appellate review, follow-on rulings, and precedent fan-out without re-querying the website.
novel_features.rationale: Reverse index of the citations table — needs the same extracted graph as the statute-citation feature plus a reverse lookup that no website page provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents tracking precedent can answer 'who cited this ruling?' instantly instead of guessing search terms.

novel_features.name: Saved-query daily digest
novel_features.description: Save a named query (court+type+keyword); on each invocation print only the JIDs newer than the last cursor. Replaces the missing RSS/email-digest on the Judicial Yuan site.
novel_features.rationale: The Judicial Yuan site has no RSS, no email digest, no webhook — Yi-Chen and Mei-Ling both check by hand weekly. A local `watchlist` table + cursor turns that into one command.
novel_features.example: judgementtw-pp-cli watch query corruption-cases --terms '貪污治罪條例' --type criminal --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to track ongoing topics or beats without polling the website yourself; the local cursor handles dedup.

novel_features.name: Watch a specific case
novel_features.description: Track a single matter (defined by court + 案號 root) for new rulings, appeals, and supplements. Prints a diff against the local change_log.
novel_features.rationale: Diffing requires a persistent JID set; the website serves one HTML page per query. Local change_log makes this a single command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Journalists and paralegals tracking specific cases get a single-command alert instead of manual tab-checking.

novel_features.name: Sentencing distribution
novel_features.description: For criminal judgments matching a statute and optional court+year, parse 主文 sentence patterns (有期徒刑X年Y月, 拘役, 罰金) and print a histogram + min/median/max.
novel_features.rationale: The Judicial Yuan publishes raw text only; sentencing analytics require regex extraction at sync into a sentences table. Existing scrapers like samttoo22 produce only .txt files.
novel_features.example: judgementtw-pp-cli sentences --statute 毒品危害防制條例 --court TPH --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: Empirical legal scholars (Persona: Prof. Wu) get sentencing-disparity analysis in one command instead of a 40-minute pandas notebook.

novel_features.name: Appeal-chain walker
novel_features.description: Walks lower court → appellate court → Supreme Court for the same matter (same parties, same 案號 root) and prints the chain.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the court-hierarchy map (built from the 41-court enum) plus 案號-root matching across tiers — neither comes from a single API call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Paralegals reconstructing case history get the full procedural chain without guessing case numbers across courts.

novel_features.name: Related-case discovery
novel_features.description: Surfaces synced judgments that cite a similar set of statutes (Jaccard similarity over the citation set), filtered to the same court tier and ±2 years.
novel_features.rationale: Similarity over citation overlap is a local computation no API exposes; needs the citations table plus the court-tier map.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Paralegals and agents asking 'more like this' get a ranked list grounded in shared legal grounds, not keyword overlap.

novel_features.name: Case-character (字別) catalog
novel_features.description: Aggregates the 字別 (case-character) field across the local corpus and groups by court, with counts and a sample JID per character.
novel_features.rationale: 字別 is the key Taiwan judicial taxonomy (e.g. 台抗, 毒抗, 訴, 簡上) and varies per court; no single API call lists it. Aggregation over the local corpus exposes the full enum.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents discovering the right 字別 to filter on get the full per-court enum in one call.

novel_features.name: Knowledge ↔ judgment linker
novel_features.description: Given an FJUDKM commentary par-token, extract its statute references and find judgments in the local store that cite the same statutes.
novel_features.rationale: The only meaningful join across the two sources — FJUDKM commentaries reference statutes; judgments cite statutes; the local citations table bridges them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Researchers reading commentary instantly find the corpus of judgments that operationalize that doctrine.

novel_features.name: Privacy-purge sweeper
novel_features.description: Re-fetches synced JIDs through the website; on a `查無資料` response (judgment removed for privacy), deletes the local row and writes an audit-log entry.
novel_features.rationale: The Judicial Yuan ToS explicitly requires local copies of removed judgments to be deleted to protect party privacy. Mechanical compliance feature; required, not optional.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Operators staying compliant with Taiwan privacy obligations don't have to write the purge logic themselves.

novel_features.name: Service-window reporter
novel_features.description: Compares current Taipei time to the 0–6 AM official-API service window; prints whether the API is reachable now and how many seconds until the next window.
novel_features.rationale: The official Judicial Yuan open-data API only serves 0–6 AM Taipei time. Even though this CLI defaults to website scraping, operators flipping on API support need to know when bulk syncs can run.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents and ops planning a bulk sync get a clear go/no-go signal without learning Taiwan's API service-window rules.

narrative.headline: Search and analyze every Taiwan court judgment offline, with a citation graph, sentencing analytics, and watchlists no judicial.gov.tw page surfaces.
narrative.value_prop: judgementTW wraps both judgment.judicial.gov.tw (judgment search across 41 courts and 5 case types) and fjudkm.judicial.gov.tw (462-topic Judicial Knowledge Base) behind one agent-native CLI. A local SQLite store turns every judgment into a queryable corpus: cross-judgment citation graphs, sentencing distributions, watchlists for ongoing cases, and appeal-chain walking — none of which the public website provides.
narrative.auth_narrative: No API key, no account, no login. judgementTW scrapes the public website with a Chrome-style User-Agent over plain HTTPS. The official open-data API path (which requires opendata.judicial.gov.tw credentials and a 6-hour token) is intentionally not enabled by default — it is only available 0–6 AM Taipei time and is more restrictive than the website. The CLI auto-purges judgments that the Judicial Yuan removes for privacy reasons (`查無資料` responses), per the website's terms of use.

quickstart.comment: Confirm both judicial.gov.tw sub-sites are reachable from your network.

quickstart.command: judgementtw-pp-cli search --court TPS --type criminal --keyword 毒品危害防制條例 --limit 10 --json
quickstart.comment: Search the Supreme Court for recent narcotics-control rulings, agent-shaped output.
Fetch a single judgment by JID, narrow to the fields an agent actually needs.

quickstart.command: judgementtw-pp-cli find --court TPH --type criminal --year 115 --limit 50 --json | jq -r '.items[].jid' | xargs -I {} judgementtw-pp-cli judgments get {} --json --select jid
quickstart.comment: Bulk-load High Court criminal rulings into the local SQLite store: find returns JIDs, xargs feeds them to judgments get.

quickstart.command: judgementtw-pp-cli cites statute 毒品危害防制條例 --article 17 --json
quickstart.comment: After syncing, ask cross-judgment questions the website cannot answer.

troubleshoots.symptom: Search returns 0 results when the website shows hits
troubleshoots.fix: ASP.NET ViewState may have rotated since your last GET. Rerun the search — the CLI re-fetches the form on every call.
Not every judgment ships a PDF. Use `get <jid> --json --select attachments` to confirm an attachment URL exists before requesting it.
All date flags expect 民國 (ROC) year. 2026 = 民國 115. The CLI also accepts `--from 115/04/01` and `--to 115/05/09`.

troubleshoots.symptom: Bulk sync hits 429 from the website
troubleshoots.fix: Lower the rate: `--rate 0.5` (one request every 2 seconds). The adaptive limiter will back off automatically on persistent 429s.

troubleshoots.symptom: Locally cached judgment is stale or removed
troubleshoots.fix: Run `judgementtw-pp-cli purge orphans` weekly. The Judicial Yuan removes judgments for privacy reasons; the CLI cleans the local copy to match.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI when an agent or operator needs to query Taiwan court judgments programmatically — single-judgment lookup, bulk corpus building, citation/precedent analysis, or watchlists for ongoing cases. It replaces the brittle Selenium scrapers used by empirical legal scholars and the manual tab-juggling done by paralegals and journalists. Do not use it for legally-binding citations (always confirm against the official Judicial Yuan record) or for redistributing corpora (the Lawsnote precedent makes commercial republication legally risky in Taiwan).

recipes.title: Build a one-year drug-case corpus and find sentencing patterns
recipes.command: judgementtw-pp-cli find --court TPH --type criminal --keyword 毒品危害防制條例 --year 115 --limit 50 --json | jq -r '.items[].jid' | xargs -I {} judgementtw-pp-cli judgments get {} --json --select jid && judgementtw-pp-cli sentences --statute 毒品危害防制條例 --court TPH --json --select statute,total_count,prison_min_months,prison_median_months,prison_max_months
recipes.explanation: find narrows to one year + topic, xargs streams JIDs into 'judgments get' to populate the local store, then sentences aggregates 主文 patterns into a histogram. --select keeps the JSON small enough for agent context.

recipes.title: Track every new ruling on an ongoing matter
recipes.explanation: On each invocation, prints only JIDs added since the last call. Cron this hourly into a Slack webhook.

recipes.title: Find the appeal chain for a Supreme Court ruling
recipes.explanation: Walks the chain across court tiers. Requires the local store to have synced the lower-court rulings first.

recipes.title: Cross-source: find judgments operationalizing a knowledge-base commentary
recipes.command: judgementtw-pp-cli knowledge search '不當得利' --limit 5 --json | jq -r '.[0].par' | xargs judgementtw-pp-cli knowledge link --json
recipes.explanation: Pipes the top FJUDKM commentary on 不當得利 (unjust enrichment) into the linker, which surfaces local judgments citing the same statutes.

recipes.title: Compact agent output for a deeply-nested response
recipes.explanation: When the result envelope is nested (find returns {total_count, page, limit, items: [...]}), dotted --select items.jid,items.jdate paths narrow JSON to three columns.
